title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-ibkr-request-retry's PR #383 review
description: Tracked, non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #383 (backend-ibkr-request-retry, the single-quick-retry addition to IBKRProvider._request), including two findings surfaced by a code-review skill pass and one surfaced by the reviewer's own latency-analysis trace. None of these block the PR: the retry logic itself was mutation-tested (disabling it, and separately removing the httpx.TimeoutException exclusion, both correctly broke the relevant tests), the full backend suite passed (1585 passed, 100% coverage), and ruff/mypy were clean. All three findings are about precision/interaction gaps in the retry policy's own latency/rate-limit analysis, not incorrect behavior observed in any test or code path.

checklist.step: `run_scanner`'s `_request` retry doesn't account for `/iserver/scanner/run`'s own externally-enforced 1-req/sec rate limit (docs/ideas.md, mirrored client-side by `_SCANNER_RUN_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`). A retryable failure (connection error or 5xx) on that specific endpoint fires a second real HTTP call only `_REQUEST_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS` (300ms) later -- well inside the 1-second window IBKR's own gateway enforces -- so the retry is plausibly rejected by that same limiter (and risks IBKR-side abuse flagging) rather than recovering. Worth deciding explicitly: either exclude `run_scanner`'s own `_request` call from the retry, or confirm (once a live gateway is available to test against) that this isn't actually a problem in practice.

`get_gateway_status`'s cold-cache path calls `_request("GET", "/iserver/auth/status")` entirely inside `_gateway_status_lock`, so the retry (up to one extra round trip plus a 300ms sleep) roughly doubles the worst-case time that lock is held -- extending contention for every other thread racing the same cache-miss/expiry (e.g. `get_analysis`'s 3-leg `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-out, which shares one `IBKRProvider` singleton and hence this one lock) during exactly the gateway-flapping window this retry targets. Worth reconsidering whether the lock needs to wrap the retrying `_request` call itself, or just the cache read/write around it.

The task's second `decisions` entry claims the retry's worst-case added cost is 'exactly one extra `_REQUEST_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS` (0.3s) plus one extra fast ... round trip' per leg -- this is imprecise for a cold-conid-cache leg in `get_analysis`'s daily/weekly fetches: `IBKRDataProvider.get_daily_ohlcv`/`get_weekly_ohlcv` each issue two sequential `_request` calls (`resolve_conid` via `_resolve_conid_or_raise`, then `get_daily_bars`/`get_weekly_bars`), so an uncached ticker's leg could independently retry both calls, adding up to ~0.6s rather than ~0.3s on that leg. Still small and bounded (and only on a cold `_conid_cache`, which has a 24h TTL), but worth a corrective `decisions` entry on the parent task noting the more precise bound.
